Do the lower hotel prices Underbook shows hold on the booking site?

Mostly yes, for the price. In a check on November 5, 2026, 17 of the 20 lower prices Underbook showed for a Christmas stay were the same price on the booking site about 40 hours later (within 5%, and within 1% at all 17); 1 was no longer offered (Super.com); 1 page could not be read (Vio.com); 1 was no longer offered (Traveluro). What varied more was the room and the cancellation terms. Across Underbook's 2 checks so far (November 3, 2026 and November 5, 2026), 36 of 40 lower prices held within 5% on the booking site, reopened 5 and 40 hours after they were shown; 1 came back higher.

So before you book a lower price, read two lines on the booking page: the room name and the cancellation terms.

The method

What was checked, and how

  • The prices: lower prices from Underbook's own recorded answers, where a booking site listed the stay 5% or more below the going rate (the price most sites agree on). Each week's hotels are picked by hand from one search run: a spread of US cities, chains and independents, small and large gaps, and several lower sites.
  • The visit: hours later, each lower listing's own link was opened in a normal Chrome browser, signed out, with nothing booked and no checkout page opened. The same was done for one mainstream listing at the going rate (Booking.com, Expedia or Hotels.com) for the same hotel, dates and party.
  • What "held" means: the booking site's page showed a price within 5% of the price Underbook showed, on the basis the page states: before tax, or the total with taxes and fees as the site reports them (a resort or destination fee may be extra).
  • The room and the terms: read on both pages: the room name, the cancellation line, and whether the price needs a sign-in.

Limits: about 20 hotels a week, one stay, US only, one read each; it shows whether the prices are real, not a rate for any site. Room names are compared as text: two sites can name one room differently, and a name match is evidence, not proof. No checkout page is opened, so taxes and fees added at checkout, and the price a signed-out traveler pays where a page says "Sign in to book", are not checked. Booking.com's all-in figures are estimates from the tax percentages its page lists. Each lower page is opened through Google Hotels' own link, the one a click there uses.

The room and the terms: the honest part

The price Underbook shows is usually the price on the site. What a price alone cannot tell you is which room it is and whether you can cancel, and in the November 5, 2026 check those differed from listing to listing:

  • Sometimes a different room. The lower price was for the same room or room type as the mainstream page at 6 of 20 hotels and a comparable one at 2, but a different room at 0, and at 7 the lower site did not name the room at all; 5 could not be compared (the lower price was gone or unreadable, or no mainstream hotel page was read). At 1 hotel the lower room was an accessible suite (the mainstream page listed the same accessible suite at its first-listed price), which a traveler who does not need one may not want to book.
  • Often no cancellation line. Free cancellation was shown on 4 of the 20 lower rates and non-refundable on 3; the other 13 did not say. At 1 hotel the non-refundable term was only in the room's name on the lower page, so read the room name too.
  • Sometimes a sign-in. 0 of the 20 lower prices said "Sign in to book".
  • Fees can sit outside the comparison. Prices are taxes and fees as each site reports them; a resort or destination fee may be extra.

Before you book a lower price

  1. Read the room name on the booking page and compare it with the room you wanted: beds, view, and whether it is an accessible room.
  2. Read the cancellation line: free cancellation and until when, or non-refundable. If the page says nothing, find the terms before you pay.
  3. Check for a sign-in or member price: the price you can book signed out is the one to compare.
  4. Check the total on the last screen, with taxes and fees as the site reports them; a resort or destination fee may be extra.

Underbook's result says whether a lower listing names the same room as one at the going rate; when it cannot, it tells you to check the room before you book. More on that: how to tell if a cheaper hotel price is the same room.

Do lower prices hold: common questions

Do the lower hotel prices Underbook shows hold on the booking site?+

Mostly, for the price. On November 5, 2026, 17 of 20 lower prices Underbook showed for a Christmas stay were within 5% on the booking site about 40 hours later, and 0 were higher. The room and the cancellation terms varied more.

Is the lower price for the same room?+

Not always. Of the 20 lower prices checked on November 5, 2026, the lower page listed the same room or room type as the mainstream booking page at 6, a comparable room at 2, a different room at 0, and named no room at 7; 5 could not be compared (the lower price was gone or unreadable, or no mainstream hotel page was read). Read the room name on the booking page before you book.

Is the lower rate refundable?+

Often the page does not say. On November 5, 2026, free cancellation was shown on 4 of the 20 lower rates, non-refundable on 3, and neither on 13. Read the cancellation line on the booking page.

How much lower was it than Booking.com, Expedia or Hotels.com?+

Where the room was the same or comparable (8 hotels), the lower page was 11.7% to 52.2% below the mainstream booking page before tax, a median of about 29%, on November 5, 2026.
